source: The rates are the ones in Jewish law and custom: a tenth (ma'aser) is the norm, a fifth (chomesh) is the ceiling the Talmud sets so that a giver does not become a taker, and less than a tenth is fine when money is tight. The ladder is Maimonides' eight levels of giving (Mishneh Torah, Laws of Gifts to the Poor 10:7-14), in plain words.
confidenceNote: Rates and levels are a tradition, not a rule this app enforces. Whether the tenth is taken from gross or after-tax income is a question rabbis answer differently; the app lets you choose and says which you chose.

rates.label: Less than a tenth
rates.plain: When money is tight, a tenth is not asked of you. Five percent here is a stand-in; type your own.

rates.label: A tenth (ma'aser)
rates.plain: The ordinary rate in Jewish practice: one dollar in ten.

rates.label: A fifth (chomesh)
rates.plain: The generous rate, and the ceiling the tradition sets: give more than this and you may need help yourself.

bases.label: After-tax income
bases.plain: What actually lands in your account. The more common reading.

bases.label: Before-tax income
bases.plain: Your salary as written. Some hold to this; it gives a bigger number.

ladder.label: Giving grudgingly
ladder.plain: You give, but you wish you had not.

ladder.label: Giving less than you should, but gladly
ladder.plain: Less than the need, with a good face.

ladder.label: Giving after being asked
ladder.plain: The full amount, once someone asks.

ladder.label: Giving before being asked
ladder.plain: You see the need and give without being asked.

ladder.label: The receiver knows you, you do not know them
ladder.plain: You give openly to someone you never learn about.

ladder.label: You know the receiver, they do not know you
ladder.plain: An anonymous gift to a named person.

ladder.label: Neither knows the other
ladder.plain: Giving to a fund or a community chest, so nobody is shamed and nobody is thanked.

ladder.label: Helping someone become self-supporting
ladder.plain: A loan, a job, a partnership, an interest-free gemach. The highest rung: a gift that ends the need.

moments.label: Yom Kippur pledge
moments.plain: Many communities ask for a yearly gift on Yom Kippur. Decide the number before the day so the ask meets a plan and not a mood.

moments.label: Gifts to the poor on Purim
moments.plain: Matanot l'evyonim: two gifts to two people in need, on the day. Any amount counts.

moments.label: Wheat money before Pesach
moments.plain: Ma'ot chitim: helping others afford their seder. Jewish family services and many shuls run a fund.

moments.label: A yahrzeit gift
moments.plain: Giving on the anniversary of a death, in the person's name. Put the date in the notes so it is not a surprise.

causes.label: Queer Jewish organizations
causes.plain: The groups that made room for you. See the Resources page.

causes.label: A Hebrew free loan fund
causes.plain: The top of the ladder: a gift that becomes a loan that becomes another loan.

causes.label: Local need: food, rent, warmth
causes.plain: A food bank, a rent fund, a shelter, a mutual-aid pot.

causes.label: Trans and queer mutual aid
causes.plain: Surgery funds, housing funds, name-change funds. Often the difference for one person.

causes.label: Your shul, minyan or havurah
causes.plain: Beyond dues: the building, the rabbi, the free High Holiday seats for the next person.

causes.label: Somewhere else
causes.plain: Anything. Say what in the note.
